parties.relationship: subcontractor business associate agreement under 45 CFR 164.504(e)(5): Meridian, a business associate of physician-practice covered entities, stands in the covered entity's place as the upstream business associate; Coastline is its offshore coding subcontractor

sentences.text: This Subcontractor Business Associate Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of March 1, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between Meridian Revenue Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company with its principal office in Atlanta, Georgia ("Meridian"), and Coastline Coding Services Private Limited, a company incorporated under the laws of India with its registered office in Chennai, Tamil Nadu ("Coastline").

Meridian provides billing, coding, and revenue cycle management services to physician practices and other health care providers (each, a "Client"), and in that role is a business associate of each Client under the HIPAA Rules.

Meridian and Coastline are parties to a Master Coding Services Agreement dated as of the Effective Date (as amended from time to time, the "Services Agreement"), under which Coastline codes and abstracts Client encounters and performs coding quality reviews for Meridian.

In performing that work, Coastline creates, receives, maintains, and transmits Protected Health Information on Meridian's behalf and is therefore Meridian's subcontractor, and a business associate in its own right, under 45 CFR 160.103.

Meridian's business associate agreements with its Clients (each, an "Upstream BAA") require Meridian to obtain satisfactory assurances from each of its subcontractors before sharing Client Protected Health Information with them, as 45 CFR 164.502(e)(1)(ii) and 164.504(e)(5) contemplate.
The parties are entering into this Agreement to give those assurances and to set the terms on which Coastline handles that information.
In consideration of the mutual promises in this Agreement and the Services Agreement, the parties agree as follows.

Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Agreement have the meanings given to them in the HIPAA Rules, including Breach, Data Aggregation, Designated Record Set, Disclosure, Health Care Operations, Individual, Minimum Necessary, Notice of Privacy Practices, Required By Law, Secretary, Security Incident, Unsecured Protected Health Information, and Use.

"HIPAA Rules" means the privacy, security, breach notification, and enforcement regulations at 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164, issued under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act.

"Meridian Platform" means the hosted encoder, document imaging, and practice management environment, reached through Meridian's virtual desktop infrastructure, in which Coastline's workforce performs the Services.

"Protected Health Information" has the meaning given in 45 CFR 160.103, limited to information that Coastline creates, receives, maintains, or transmits on Meridian's behalf, including information about Clients' patients.
"Services" means the coding, abstraction, and coding quality review services Coastline performs under the Services Agreement.

"Subcontractor" means any person or entity, other than a member of Coastline's workforce, to which Coastline delegates a function, activity, or service that involves creating, receiving, maintaining, or transmitting Protected Health Information.
Coastline will not use or further disclose Protected Health Information except as expressly permitted or required by this Agreement or as Required By Law.

Coastline shall implement and maintain appropriate administrative, physical, and technical safeguards to prevent any use or disclosure of Protected Health Information not provided for by this Agreement.
Coastline shall comply with Subpart C of 45 CFR Part 164 with respect to electronic Protected Health Information.
Coastline shall work with Protected Health Information solely within the Meridian Platform and shall not download, print, photograph, or store it on any local device or removable media.

Coastline shall require multi-factor authentication for every workforce member who logs in to the Meridian Platform and shall disable a member's credentials within twenty-four hours after the member no longer needs them.
Coastline shall maintain ISO/IEC 27001 certification for its delivery centers and shall give Meridian a copy of each surveillance and recertification audit report.
Coastline shall report to Meridian any use or disclosure of Protected Health Information not provided for by this Agreement of which it becomes aware.
Coastline shall report to Meridian any Breach of Unsecured Protected Health Information that it discovers, as 45 CFR 164.410 requires.

Coastline shall report to Meridian any Security Incident of which it becomes aware, except that no report is required for unsuccessful attempts, such as pings, port scans, and blocked log-on attempts, that do not result in unauthorized access to Protected Health Information.
Coastline shall notify Meridian of any Breach without unreasonable delay after discovering it.
In no event shall Coastline give notice of a Breach later than seventy-two (72) hours after discovery of the Breach.

Coastline's notice of a Breach shall identify each Individual whose Unsecured Protected Health Information has been, or is reasonably believed by Coastline to have been, accessed, acquired, used, or disclosed in the Breach, to the extent Coastline is able to do so.

Coastline shall provide Meridian with any other available information that Meridian or the affected Client needs to notify Individuals under 45 CFR 164.404(c), and shall supplement that information as further facts become known.
Coastline shall cooperate with Meridian's investigation of any Breach, including by preserving relevant system logs and making knowledgeable personnel available for interviews.

Meridian, in consultation with the affected Client, will decide whether and how Individuals, the Secretary, and the media are told of a Breach, and Coastline shall not contact any of them about a Breach unless Meridian directs it to do so.

Coastline shall reimburse Meridian and the affected Client for the reasonable costs of notifying Individuals of a Breach caused by Coastline or a Subcontractor, including credit monitoring, call center, and forensic investigation costs.

Coastline shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits Protected Health Information on Coastline's behalf agrees to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Coastline under this Agreement.

Coastline shall set out each Subcontractor's obligations regarding Protected Health Information in a written business associate agreement signed before that Subcontractor first receives any Protected Health Information.

Coastline shall not permit any Subcontractor to receive Protected Health Information without Meridian's prior approval, and Coastline remains responsible to Meridian for each Subcontractor's acts and omissions.
Coastline shall make Protected Health Information in a Designated Record Set available to Meridian so that Meridian or the applicable Client can respond to an Individual's request for access.

Coastline shall deliver the requested Protected Health Information within five (5) business days after Meridian's request, in the form and format Meridian specifies, so that the applicable Client can meet its access obligations under 45 CFR 164.524.
Coastline shall promptly forward to Meridian any request for access that it receives directly from an Individual and shall not respond to the Individual unless Meridian so directs.
Coastline shall make Protected Health Information in a Designated Record Set available to Meridian for amendment.

Coastline shall incorporate any amendment to Protected Health Information that Meridian directs, within ten (10) business days after receiving the direction, as necessary for the applicable Client to satisfy 45 CFR 164.526.
Coastline shall promptly forward to Meridian any request for amendment that it receives directly from an Individual.
Coastline shall document its disclosures of Protected Health Information and make available to Meridian the information required to provide an accounting of disclosures.

Coastline shall provide the information Meridian requests for an accounting of disclosures within ten (10) business days after the request, so that the applicable Client can respond to the Individual as 45 CFR 164.528 requires.
Coastline shall promptly forward to Meridian any request for an accounting that it receives directly from an Individual.

To the extent Coastline carries out any obligation of Meridian or a Client under Subpart E of 45 CFR Part 164, Coastline shall comply with the requirements of Subpart E that apply to Meridian or that Client in performing the obligation.

Coastline shall give the Secretary access to its internal practices, books, and records concerning Protected Health Information whenever the Secretary requests them to determine Meridian's, a Client's, or Coastline's compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
Unless the law forbids it, Coastline shall promptly tell Meridian of any request it receives from the Secretary and shall give Meridian a copy of the materials it produces in response.
Meridian, and not Coastline, decides which Client records are released to Coastline's work queue.
Coastline may use or disclose Protected Health Information only as necessary to perform the Services for Meridian under the Services Agreement.
Coastline may use or disclose Protected Health Information as Required By Law.
Coastline may use Protected Health Information for its proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities.

Coastline may disclose Protected Health Information for its own management, administration, and legal purposes where the law requires the disclosure, or where Coastline first obtains the recipient's reasonable assurance that it will keep the information confidential, will make no further disclosure except as the law requires or for the purpose of the original disclosure, and will tell Coastline of any known compromise of the information's confidentiality.
Coastline shall limit its uses and disclosures of, and requests for, Protected Health Information to the minimum necessary, consistent with the minimum necessary policies Meridian communicates to it.
Coastline shall not de-identify Protected Health Information, aggregate it with data of its other customers, or create any derivative data set from it.

Coastline may not use or disclose Protected Health Information in any manner that would violate Subpart E of 45 CFR Part 164 if done by Meridian or the applicable Client, other than for the management, administration, and legal purposes this Article expressly permits.

Meridian shall notify Coastline of any limitation in a Client's notice of privacy practices under 45 CFR 164.520, to the extent the limitation affects Coastline's use or disclosure of Protected Health Information.

Meridian shall notify Coastline of any change in, or revocation of, an Individual's permission to use or disclose Protected Health Information, to the extent the change affects Coastline's use or disclosure of that information.

Meridian shall notify Coastline of any restriction on the use or disclosure of Protected Health Information that a Client has agreed to or must honor under 45 CFR 164.522, to the extent the restriction affects Coastline.

Meridian shall notify Coastline of any term of an Upstream BAA that is stricter than this Agreement and affects the Services, and Coastline shall follow that term from the date it receives the notice.
Meridian shall not ask Coastline to handle Protected Health Information in any manner that would be impermissible under Subpart E of 45 CFR Part 164 for the applicable Client.
This Agreement takes effect on the Effective Date and continues until the Services Agreement expires or is terminated.
Termination of this Agreement for any reason also ends the Services Agreement to the extent the Services Agreement calls for Coastline to handle Protected Health Information.

Meridian may terminate this Agreement and the Services Agreement if Meridian determines that Coastline has violated a material term of this Agreement and Coastline has not cured the violation within thirty (30) days after written notice from Meridian.
Meridian may suspend Coastline's access to the Meridian Platform while any violation of this Agreement by Coastline remains uncured.
Meridian may terminate this Agreement immediately if a Client withdraws its approval of Coastline or ends its Upstream BAA because of Coastline's conduct.

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason, Coastline shall return to Meridian or, if Meridian so elects, destroy all Protected Health Information that Coastline still maintains in any form.

Coastline shall retain no copies of Protected Health Information once it has been returned or destroyed, except that if Meridian agrees that returning or destroying particular information is infeasible, Coastline shall extend the protections of this Agreement to that information and limit further uses and disclosures to the purposes that make its return or destruction infeasible, for as long as Coastline maintains it.

Coastline shall obtain the return or destruction of Protected Health Information held by its Subcontractors and shall deliver to Meridian an officer's certificate confirming completion within thirty (30) days after termination or expiration.
Any provision of this Agreement that by its nature is meant to continue after termination survives termination.
Each reference in this Agreement to a section of the HIPAA Rules refers to that section as in effect from time to time.
If the HIPAA Rules change in a way that affects this Agreement, the parties shall negotiate in good faith to amend this Agreement to the extent needed to keep it compliant.
Any ambiguity in this Agreement shall be resolved in favor of a meaning that allows Meridian, each Client, and Coastline to comply with the HIPAA Rules.
If this Agreement conflicts with the Services Agreement on any matter concerning Protected Health Information, this Agreement controls.
The limitations of liability in the Services Agreement do not apply to Coastline's liability for breach of this Agreement.

Coastline shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Meridian from third-party claims, regulatory penalties, and reasonable costs arising from Coastline's or a Subcontractor's breach of this Agreement.
Nothing in this Agreement gives any person other than Meridian and Coastline any right or remedy.
This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Georgia, except where federal law controls.
The parties may sign this Agreement in counterparts and by electronic signature, and each counterpart is an original.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have signed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
MERIDIAN REVENUE PARTNERS, LLC
By: Danielle Okafor
Title: Chief Compliance Officer
Date: March 1, 2026
COASTLINE CODING SERVICES PRIVATE LIMITED
By: Arvind Raghunathan
Title: Managing Director
Date: March 1, 2026

sentences.text: This Master Coding Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of March 1, 2026 (the "Effective Date") by and between Coastline Coding Services Private Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 of India, with its registered office at Plot 14, Old Mahabalipuram Road, Sholinganallur, Chennai 600119, India ("Coastline"), and Meridian Revenue Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company with its principal office at 1180 Peachtree Street, Suite 2200, Atlanta, Georgia 30309 ("Customer").
Customer provides billing and revenue cycle management services to physician practices and is a business associate of each of them under the HIPAA Rules.
Coastline provides credentialed medical coding, abstraction, and coding audit services from delivery centers in India.
Customer wishes to engage Coastline to code the encounters of Customer's clients, and Coastline is willing to do so on the terms of this Agreement.
The parties therefore agree as follows.
Capitalized terms used in this Agreement have the meanings given in this Section 1 or where they first appear in quotation marks.
"Applicable Law" means all laws and regulations that apply to a party's performance of this Agreement, including the HIPAA Rules and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
"Client" means a physician practice or other health care provider that has engaged Customer for billing or revenue cycle services and whose encounters Customer submits to Coastline for coding.
"Customer Data" means all data, documents, and images that Customer or a Client makes available to Coastline, together with all Work Product, including Customer PHI.
"Customer PHI" means Protected Health Information that Coastline creates, receives, maintains, or transmits on behalf of Customer in connection with this Agreement.
"Customer Platform" means Customer's hosted encoder, document imaging, and practice management environment, reached through Customer's virtual desktop infrastructure.
"Delivery Centers" means Coastline's facilities in Chennai and Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India, and any other facility Customer approves in writing.

"HIPAA Rules" means the regulations at 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164 issued under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, as amended by the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act.
"Personnel" means Coastline's employees, and any individual contractors Customer has approved, who perform Services from a Delivery Center.

"Protected Health Information", "Breach", "Designated Record Set", "Individual", "Required By Law", "Secretary", and "Unsecured Protected Health Information" have the meanings given in the HIPAA Rules.

"Security Incident" means the attempted or successful unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or destruction of Customer Data, or interference with system operations in an information system that holds Customer Data.
"Services" means the professional fee and facility coding, abstraction, charge review, and coding audit services described in an SOW.
"SOW" means a statement of work signed by both parties that describes specific Services, specialties, volumes, Turnaround Times, and Fees.
"Subcontractor" means any third party, other than Personnel, that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits Customer PHI on Coastline's behalf.
"Turnaround Time" means the period between release of a chart to Coastline's work queue on the Customer Platform and Coastline's completed coding of that chart.
"Work Product" means the codes, abstracts, provider queries, audit findings, and other output Coastline produces in performing the Services.
Coastline shall perform the Services described in each SOW in accordance with this Agreement.
Each SOW forms part of this Agreement when signed by both parties.
Coastline shall not begin work under an SOW until both parties have signed it.
Customer has no minimum volume commitment unless an SOW states one.

Coastline shall assign codes in accordance with the ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, the CPT and HCPCS code sets, National Correct Coding Initiative edits, and any Client-specific coding policies Customer supplies.
Coastline shall not assign a code that the clinical documentation does not support, whether the documentation comes from a template, a copied note, or an encounter form.

Where documentation is incomplete or ambiguous, Coastline shall place the chart on hold and submit a compliant provider query through the Customer Platform rather than assume a diagnosis or procedure.
Customer is responsible for routing queries to the treating provider and returning the responses to Coastline's work queue.
Customer shall give Coastline accounts on the Customer Platform for the Personnel Coastline designates, together with encoder licenses and the Client coding policies that apply to the work.
Customer remains solely responsible for final claim review, claim submission, and its contractual commitments to Clients.
The service levels in this Section 3 apply from the end of the ramp-up period stated in each SOW.
Coastline shall complete coding of at least ninety-five percent (95%) of charts within the Turnaround Time stated in the applicable SOW, measured monthly.
Unless an SOW states otherwise, the Turnaround Time is forty-eight (48) hours for professional fee charts and seventy-two (72) hours for facility charts.
Coastline shall maintain coding accuracy of at least ninety-five percent (95%), measured by Customer's monthly sample review of not less than two percent (2%) of completed charts.
Coastline shall correct any chart found to be miscoded at no additional charge.

If Coastline misses a service level in any month, Customer is entitled to a credit of five percent (5%) of the Fees for that month for each missed service level, up to a total of fifteen percent (15%).
Service credits are applied against the next invoice and are Customer's exclusive monetary remedy for missed service levels.
Customer shall pay the fees set out in each SOW (the "Fees").
Fees are charged per completed chart at the rates in the applicable SOW and are fixed for the first twenty-four (24) months of the Term.

After that period Coastline may increase its rates once per contract year on ninety (90) days' notice, by no more than the lesser of four percent (4%) and the change in India's Consumer Price Index over the prior twelve months.
No Fee is payable for a chart on hold for a provider query until its coding is complete.
Coastline shall invoice monthly in arrears in United States dollars.
Customer shall pay each undisputed invoice within forty-five (45) days after receipt.

Customer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Coastline of the dispute before the due date, and the parties shall work together to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days.
Each party is responsible for its own income taxes.

If Applicable Law requires Customer to withhold tax from any payment, Customer shall withhold the required amount, pay it to the appropriate authority, and give Coastline the official receipt so that Coastline may claim a credit under the India-United States income tax treaty.

Once in each contract year, Customer or an independent accountant bound by confidentiality may examine the invoices, chart-count reports, and time entries that support the Fees, on at least thirty (30) days' notice.

Customer bears the cost of each such examination unless it reveals an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), in which case Coastline shall refund the overcharge and reimburse the reasonable cost of the examination.
Coastline is solely responsible for the hiring, supervision, compensation, and discipline of its Personnel.
Coastline shall perform the Services only from the Delivery Centers.

Coastline shall not permit Customer Data to be viewed, stored, or processed in any country other than India and the United States, and shall not relocate the Services to a new facility without Customer's prior approval.
Remote work by Personnel is permitted only under a remote work plan that Customer has approved in advance.

Coastline shall assign to the Services only coders who hold a current CPC, CCS, CCS-P, or equivalent credential from AAPC or AHIMA and who have at least two years of coding experience in the assigned specialty.

Before assigning any individual to the Services, Coastline shall complete a criminal background check, verification of education and employment history, and an identity check, and shall repeat the criminal check every two years.
Coastline shall train all Personnel on HIPAA privacy and security requirements before they receive Customer Platform accounts and at least annually after that.
Coastline represents that neither it nor any of its Personnel is excluded from participation in any federal health care program.

Coastline shall screen all Personnel against the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities and the SAM.gov exclusion database before assignment and monthly after that, and shall remove any excluded individual from the Services immediately.
Coastline shall not delegate any part of the Services to a third party without Customer's prior approval.
Coastline is responsible for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors as though they were Coastline's own.
Coastline's obligations regarding Subcontractors that handle Customer PHI are set out in Section B.5 of Exhibit B.
Coastline shall designate a dedicated account manager who will attend monthly operational reviews with Customer and quarterly business reviews with Customer's executive sponsor.
Customer hosts the Customer Platform, and Personnel perform the Services by remote connection to it from the Delivery Centers.
Customer shall host, maintain, and administer the Customer Platform at its own cost, including provisioning and revoking Personnel accounts at Coastline's request.
Turnaround Times are suspended for any period during which the Customer Platform is unavailable to Coastline for reasons outside Coastline's control.
Coastline shall implement and maintain appropriate administrative, physical, and technical safeguards to prevent any use or disclosure of Customer PHI not provided for by this Agreement.
Coastline shall comply with Subpart C of 45 CFR Part 164 (the "Security Rule") with respect to electronic Customer PHI.

Coastline shall work with Customer Data solely within the Customer Platform and shall not download, print, photograph, or store Customer Data on any local device, personal email account, or removable media.
Coastline shall require multi-factor authentication for every Personnel login, restrict production floors to badge-controlled entry, and prohibit mobile phones and personal devices on those floors.
Coastline shall maintain ISO/IEC 27001 certification for each Delivery Center and shall give Customer its current certificate and the summary of each surveillance audit on request.
Coastline shall supply and maintain, at its own cost, the workstations, network connectivity, and backup power its Personnel need to reach the Customer Platform from the Delivery Centers.
Each party shall bear its own costs of complying with this Section 6.
This Section 7 allocates rights in Customer Data and Work Product between the parties.
As between the parties, Customer owns all right, title, and interest in Customer Data and Work Product.
Customer grants Coastline a non-exclusive, non-transferable license during the Term to access and process Customer Data as necessary to provide the Services.
Coastline acquires no ownership interest in Customer Data or Work Product.
Coastline shall not de-identify Customer PHI or create, sell, or license any aggregated or de-identified data set derived from Customer Data.
Coastline may compile statistics about the productivity and accuracy of its own Personnel, provided that the statistics contain no Customer PHI and do not name Customer or any Client.
Neither party shall refer to the other party by name or logo in any publicity without the other party's prior consent.
Each party may receive the other's Confidential Information in performing this Agreement.

"Confidential Information" means non-public information that one party discloses to the other in connection with this Agreement and that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential, including pricing and the terms of this Agreement.
Customer PHI is governed by Exhibit B rather than this Section 8.

Confidential Information does not include information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, that the receiving party already knew without restriction, or that the receiving party develops independently.

The receiving party shall protect the disclosing party's Confidential Information with at least reasonable care and shall limit disclosure to its employees, Personnel, and professional advisers who need to know it for this Agreement and are bound by confidentiality duties at least as protective as this Section 8.
A party may disclose Confidential Information when compelled by law or court order, after giving the other party prompt notice where the law allows.
Each party represents that it has the authority to enter into this Agreement.
Coastline warrants that it will perform the Services in a professional manner, by qualified Personnel, and in accordance with the coding standards in Section 2.2.
Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is re-performance of the affected Services at no charge, together with any service credits under Section 3.3.
Customer warrants that it has obtained from each Client the authority needed to share that Client's records with Coastline for the Services.
EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, COASTLINE DISCLAIMS ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
Customer remains responsible for the claims it submits to payers, and Coastline does not guarantee any particular reimbursement outcome.
The indemnities in this Section 10 are subject to Section 11 except where Section 11 states otherwise.

Coastline shall defend Customer against any third-party claim, government investigation, or payer recoupment arising from Coastline's gross negligence, willful misconduct, violation of Applicable Law, or breach of Section 8 or Exhibit B, and shall pay the resulting damages, fines, penalties, settlements, and reasonable attorneys' fees.

Customer shall defend Coastline against any third-party claim arising from the content of Client records or from Customer's instructions to Coastline, and shall pay the resulting damages, settlements, and reasonable attorneys' fees.
The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt notice of the claim, sole control of its defense and settlement, and reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.
The indemnifying party shall not settle any claim in a way that imposes an obligation on the indemnified party without that party's consent.
This Section 11 applies to all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise.
Neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
Except as provided in Section 11.3, each party's total liability under this Agreement is limited to the Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months before the event giving rise to the claim.

Coastline's liability for breach of Section 8 or Exhibit B, and for its indemnity obligations under Section 10.1, is limited to three times the Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months before the event giving rise to the claim.
Section 11.1 does not limit recovery of the reasonable costs of investigating a Breach, notifying affected Individuals, and providing credit monitoring, which the parties agree are direct damages.
Coastline shall maintain the insurance described in this Section 12 throughout the Term and for two years after it ends, with insurers rated A- or better by AM Best.
Coastline shall carry professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with limits of at least USD 5,000,000 per claim.

Coastline shall carry network security and privacy liability insurance with limits of at least USD 5,000,000 per claim, covering regulatory defense and penalties and the costs of responding to a Breach.
Coastline shall carry commercial general liability insurance with limits of at least USD 2,000,000 per occurrence.
Coastline shall name Customer as an additional insured on its general liability policy and shall deliver certificates of insurance on the Effective Date and at each renewal.
This Agreement may be ended only as provided in this Section 13.

This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of three (3) years, after which it renews automatically for successive one-year periods unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the current period ends (together, the "Term").

Customer may terminate this Agreement or any SOW by written notice if Coastline breaches a material term of this Agreement, including any term of Exhibit B, and does not cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice from Customer.
Customer may suspend any affected SOW while a breach of Exhibit B by Coastline remains uncured.

Coastline may terminate this Agreement by written notice if Customer fails to pay undisputed Fees within sixty (60) days after the due date and does not pay them within fifteen (15) days after receiving a reminder.
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any SOW for convenience on ninety (90) days' notice.
Customer shall pay for Services completed through the effective date of any expiration or termination.
Upon expiration or termination, Coastline shall finish coding any chart already in progress unless Customer directs otherwise, and Customer shall pay for that work.
At Customer's request, Coastline shall provide transition assistance for up to ninety (90) days at the rates then in effect.
Coastline's obligations regarding Customer PHI upon expiration or termination are set out in Section B.8 of Exhibit B.
